object_description: elongated nine-storey cuboid with stacked table-like precast frames and escape balconies
geometry_property: escape balconies along the long sides
second ground floor at the lower level
design_condition: the elongated cuboid turns its narrow side to the street and is positioned so that two differently proportioned outdoor spaces form in the depth of the plot

positive: The established urban pattern of point high-rises is further developed as a large-scale pattern
The organising large-scale form makes sense in the heterogeneous environment
It creates space for further structural developments
The positioning forms two differently proportioned outdoor spaces in the depth of the plot
These thematise the self-evident nature of the building and support its self-confident expression
A simple system of stacked table-like precast frames structures all facades in uniform proportions
The slightly conical supports emphasise the stacking theme and create a delicate, almost fragile expression
Deep-set windows and escape balconies create a differentiated spatial grid
The large forecourt is logically designed as a hard square structured with the skylights below
The concept of a second ground floor on the lower level corresponds to the external spatial structure
It creates a convincing functional prelude to the building
The first six upper floors are well structured with classrooms of different sizes
The interconnectable classrooms are given good and usable room proportions
The access area open to the facade provides an outdoor connection on each floor
It creates an attractive location for the flexibly configurable learning islands
The project continues the large-scale urban idea in an interesting way
It consolidates into a convincing arrangement of the outdoor space around the building
negative: The desired public square character lacks adequate design and a convincing connection to the ground floor
The main entrance faces the street in a covered forecourt that almost competes with the large square
The extra-wide staircase obscures the values and desired moods of the two outdoor spaces
The rear floor plan area of the lower level leads to unattractive and poorly lit room sequences
The spatial connection to the upper floor seems random and lacks an overall concept across the two floors
The upper entrance floor has a somewhat small-scale layout despite the spacious foyer
The possibility of connecting both administration floors with zenithal lighting has not been exploited
The access corridor there appears hermetic and closed
The main circulation reducing in width towards the top is neither functional nor spatially comprehensible
With this building height stair use is unrealistic, so the staircase will not be used equally on all floors
The number of lifts is too low and the fire protection vestibules are missing
The larger shaft room at the top offers no major advantages
The required external fire protection glazing makes a more economical solution impossible
The compact high-rise achieves unfavourable floor space ratios
Large facade development, high glazing and elaborate escape balconies drive costs
Construction costs are in the upper segment
The internal implementation is not convincing
